:::{#exr-fubini-joint-mixed-infinite}

#### Mixed case, infinite discrete support

Let $Y$ be Geometric on $\{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$
with $\P(Y = y) = (1-q)\,q^y$ for a fixed $q \in (0, 1)$ and,
given $Y = y$, let $X \mid Y = y \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0,\, y+1)$.
Unlike @exr-fubini-joint-mixed, $Y$'s range here is countably infinite.

Compute $\E{X}$.

:::

::: {.solution}

Compute $\E{X}$ using @cor-fubini-joint with $\measure_X = \text{Lebesgue measure}$,
$\measure_Y = \text{counting measure}$, and $h(x, y) = x$.

The joint density w.r.t. Lebesgue $\times$ counting measure is

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{X,Y}(x, y) &= f_{X \mid Y}(x \mid y)\,\P(Y = y) \\
&= \frac{(1-q)\,q^y}{y+1}
\end{aligned}
$$

for $x \in [0, y+1]$.

Since $h(x, y) = x \ge 0$ on this support, condition (a) holds,
so @cor-fubini-joint (via Tonelli's theorem) guarantees the now-infinite
sum-of-integrals expression is valid --- unlike in @exr-fubini-joint-mixed,
this Fubini--Tonelli justification is required because the sum is infinite rather than finite.

By @cor-fubini-joint (mixed case):

$$
\ba
\E{X}
&= \sum_{y=0}^{\infty} \int_0^{y+1} x\,f_{X,Y}(x,\,y)\,dx
&& \text{(joint-distribution form of Fubini--Tonelli, mixed case)}
\\&= \sum_{y=0}^{\infty} \frac{(1-q)\,q^y}{y+1} \int_0^{y+1} x\,dx
&& \text{(} f_{X,Y}(x, y) \text{ is constant in } x \text{ on } [0, y+1] \text{)}
\\&= \sum_{y=0}^{\infty} \frac{(1-q)\,q^y}{y+1} \cd \frac{(y+1)^2}{2}
&& \text{(integrate)}
\\&= \frac{1-q}{2} \sum_{y=0}^{\infty} (y+1)\,q^y
&& \text{(cancel } y + 1 \text{; factor out } \tfrac{1-q}{2} \text{)}
\\&= \frac{1-q}{2} \paren{\sum_{y=0}^{\infty} y\,q^y + \sum_{y=0}^{\infty} q^y}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\&= \frac{1-q}{2} \paren{\frac{q}{(1-q)^2} + \frac{1}{1-q}}
&& \text{(geometric-series facts)}
\\&= \frac{1-q}{2} \cd \frac{q + (1-q)}{(1-q)^2}
&& \text{(common denominator)}
\\&= \frac{1-q}{2} \cd \frac{1}{(1-q)^2}
&& \text{(simplify the numerator)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2(1-q)}
&& \text{(cancel } 1 - q \text{)}
\ea
$$

using the same geometric-series facts as @exr-fubini-joint-disc-infinite
(e.g. @CaseBerg01).

As a check using the law of iterated expectations (@thm-lie)
and the expectation of a linear function (@cor-linearity-affine):
$\E{X \mid Y=y} = \frac{y+1}{2}$ (the mean of $\mathrm{Uniform}(0,y+1)$)
and $\E{Y} = \frac{q}{1-q}$ (the mean of this Geometric distribution;
@CaseBerg01), so:

$$
\ba
\E{X} &= \E{\E{X \mid Y}}
&& \text{(law of iterated expectations)}
\\&= \E{\frac{Y+1}{2}}
&& \text{(} \E{X \mid Y = y} = \tfrac{y+1}{2} \text{)}
\\&= \frac{\E{Y} + 1}{2}
&& \text{(expectation of a linear function of one random variable)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2}\paren{\frac{q}{1-q} + 1}
&& \text{(substitute } \E{Y} \text{)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2} \cd \frac{q + (1-q)}{1-q}
&& \text{(common denominator)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2(1-q)}
&& \text{(simplify the numerator)}
\ea
$$

matching.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false

q <- 0.5
exact_ex <- 1 / (2 * (1 - q))

n_trunc <- 2000
y_vals <- 0:n_trunc
py_vals <- (1 - q) * q^y_vals
cond_mean_x <- (y_vals + 1) / 2
trunc_ex <- sum(cond_mean_x * py_vals)

pander::pander(tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("exact (closed form)", "truncated sum-of-integrals"),
  value = round(c(exact_ex, trunc_ex), 6)
))
```

With $q = `r q`$, the truncated sum-of-integrals matches the closed form
$\frac{1}{2(1-q)} = `r round(exact_ex, 4)`$.

:::
